_comment: generated by libs/casino-client/scripts/gen-receipts-export-fixture.ts — do not hand-edit. Cross-language fixture for the receipts export (ADR 0022 / design §12.3): each case carries one `export` document and the facts a verifier must read back out of it. Every key is fixed — seeds, request ids, sequences and timestamps — so two renders are byte-identical. `expected.frames[].origin` is null both when the frame class has no origin field and when the field is STEP_ORIGIN_UNSPECIFIED, because proto3 omits a zero enum from the wire entirely. The three hilo-* cases share one commitment: a SYSTEM step occupies an action index but has no archived command, so it cannot change the fold. The two forced-settle cases are different rounds and commit over their own command sets — a swept RoundEnded names no command at all (nothing produced the settling step), while a transcript-cap RoundEnded names the command whose action was substituted, because that command WAS archived. The two crash-* cases cover the settle command that stopped being replay-constant: a manual round's CashOut carries the crash.v1 arm with the tick the player claimed, so its bytes — and the commitment over them — depend on a value chosen at send time, while an auto round pre-commits its target in the bet and archives no cashout command at all. The crash-two-tab-rejection case adds the round-scoped refusal: two tabs of one session share one store, tab A settles the round and tab B is refused ROUND_CLOSED on a CommandRejected that NAMES the round (so it is a round frame, and tab B's command is exported with it), yet the commitment equals the crash-manual-claimed one — a refusal is not an acknowledgement, so the refused command contributes no index and no preimage bytes. Its accepted frames are the only ones carrying received_at_unix_ms; the others keep the pre-field shape a reader must also handle, since CommandAccepted is a durable client_outbox row. The four per-arm cases exist so a command-body reader is pinned on EVERY oneof arm rather than on the arms the earlier cases happened to use: mines-plain covers mines_v1_bet / mines_v1_action(reveal, including tile 0, the value proto3 implicit presence would erase) / mines_v1_cash_out; hydra-full-vocabulary covers hydra_v1_bet and ALL FIVE PlayerAction arms (fight, physical_attack, magic_attack, drink_potion, drink_mana) plus hydra_v1_cash_out — note fight and physical_attack are distinct arms the sequencer maps to ONE engine action, so a rule over them must be set membership and never a bijection; plinko-client-settled covers plinko_v1_cash_out, the settle the sweep case never receives; and hilo-lower-cashout covers the hilo lower arm, which the hilo-plain case's `higher` does not. crash-deadline-notice adds the advisory RoundDeadlineReached (payload tag 112) to the crash manual round: it names the round on its signed round_id and no command, carries no action index, and so is exported with the round while its commitment stays crash-manual-claimed.
